title: Convexity and Jensen's Inequality

los.vardeez: Jensen's inequality. Remember: the value of convexity increases with bond volatility and time to maturity

selectors.name: Jensen's inequality on bond prices
selectors.what: Direction of Jensen's inequality for bonds: because price is convex in the rate, the expected price E[1/(1+r)] exceeds the price at the expected rate 1/(1+E[r]); hence forward rates lie below expected rates once volatility is added.

selectors.name: Convexity value increases with volatility
selectors.what: The value of convexity (the lowering of forward rates below expected rates) rises with interest rate volatility; with zero volatility expectations alone fix the term structure.

selectors.name: Convexity value increases with maturity
selectors.what: The value of convexity grows with time to maturity, so forward rates bend down more at longer terms even with equal per-step volatility; a statement that it falls with maturity is a flip.

notSelected: MR-13 a (role of expectations in the term structure), the risk-neutral tree arithmetic of MR-13 b beyond the volatility effect, and MR-13 d (return decomposition, expected return for a risk-averse investor, Sharpe ratio, forward rate decomposition) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer; calculations are explicitly deprioritised.
